Akita (Akita-shi) is the principal port and the capital city of Japan's Akita Prefecture (Honshu Island's Tohoku region), with population around 315,000. The seaport is on the Sea of Japan (to the west), while the Omono River runs through downtown.

Port Akita (locode JPAXT) is officially classified as "Major Port" and has total land area approx 663 hectares (6,6 km2). During Edo/Tokugawa period (1603-1868), Akita was a major port on the coastal trade route from Osaka to Hokkaido. During the Meiji period (1868-1912) was finished a breakwater (in 1885) that was further expanded in 1902.

Port Tsuchizakiko was designated as “secondary port” in 1910. When in 1941 Tsuchizaki was merged with Akita, the port was officially renamed “Akita Port”. Most of its facilities were heavily damaged during the US air raids in August 1945. After WW2 (1939-1945), the seaport was improved. Its breakwater was extended via the sinking of damaged Japanese military vessels (including the Matsu-class destroyers Take and Momo). The Japanese government classed Akita as “major port” in 1951 and as “special port” in 1962. Its Customs Office opened in 1964, allowing international shipping trade. Northern Port's extension was completed in 1970.

Akita is normally a docked port call, with cruise ships using Nakajima Pier beside the Akita Cruise Terminal. The port area itself is easy to explore on foot, but central Akita is not a practical walk from the ship. For the main city sights, plan on using a local bus, taxi or any transfer provided for your particular cruise call.

Overall: Independent sightseeing is practical, but it requires some transport planning. Staying around Port Tower Selion is very easy independently; central Akita is also straightforward once you reach Akita Station. Longer trips to Oga or Kakunodate need considerably more attention to transport and return times.

Getting from the Cruise Port

  • Berth: Cruise ships normally use Nakajima Pier, where the Akita Cruise Terminal handles arriving passengers.
  • Port Tower Selion: About 1 km (0.6 mi) from the cruise berth, roughly a 10–15 minute walk. This is the easiest attraction to visit directly from the ship.
  • Akita Station and city center: Allow about 20–25 minutes by road from the port area.
  • Public bus: Akita Chuo Kotsu's Selion Line, including route 115, connects the Selion area with Akita Station West Exit. Services are not especially frequent, particularly on weekends, so check the return timetable before relying on the bus.
  • Taxi: The simplest independent choice when several people are traveling together or when the port call is short.

Important: Older Akita cruise guides may mention a dedicated train between Akita Port and Akita Station. Cruise passenger trains ended after the 2025 fiscal year, and the Akita Port railway branch was abolished on July 1, 2026. Do not plan a visit around the former cruise train.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Central Akita and Senshu Park

Allow about 4–5 hours including port transfers. This is the best independent choice for a first visit. Start around Akita Station and combine Senshu Park, the former Kubota Castle grounds, Akita Museum of Art and one or two smaller cultural attractions.

Senshu Park is about a 10-minute walk from Akita Station. The lower park and castle gates are easy to reach, while the climb toward the reconstructed Osumiyagura turret involves slopes and some steps. Nearby cultural stops include the Akita City Folk Performing Arts Heritage Center, commonly called Neburinagashi Kan, where the city's Kanto lantern tradition is presented, and the distinctive Red Brick Folk Museum.

Independent sightseeing: Easy once in the city center. Use a taxi or the Selion bus between port and Akita Station rather than trying to walk from the ship.

Port Tower Selion and the Akita Port Area

Allow 1–2 hours. This is the simplest option for passengers who want to remain close to the ship. Port Tower Selion has a free observation level approximately 100 meters above the ground with views across the Sea of Japan, Akita and, in clear weather, the surrounding mountains and Oga Peninsula.

The surrounding Michi-no-Eki Akita Port complex includes Selion Garden for regional products and the enclosed Selion Rista space. It works particularly well for a short call, poor weather or passengers who prefer minimal transport.

Independent sightseeing: Very easy. The principal sights are within walking distance of the cruise terminal.

Oga Peninsula and Namahage Culture

Allow roughly 4–5 hours. The Namahage Museum on the Oga Peninsula is about a 50-minute drive from the Akita Port area. It displays the distinctive masks and traditions associated with Oga's Namahage, while the neighboring Oga Shinzan Folklore Museum presents demonstrations of the custom inside a traditional house.

Public transport from the cruise terminal requires considerably more time and connections, so this is better approached by organized excursion, pre-arranged vehicle or taxi. Adding extensive sightseeing around the Oga Peninsula increases the time requirement further.

Independent sightseeing: Possible with pre-arranged transport; organized excursion recommended for most cruise passengers.

Kakunodate Samurai District

Allow at least 5–6 hours and preferably a long port call. Kakunodate is a preserved castle town known for its samurai residences and historic streets. From Akita Station, the fastest Akita Shinkansen journey is about 42 minutes, followed by approximately 15–20 minutes on foot from Kakunodate Station to the main samurai district.

A typical walk through Kakunodate covers about 5 km (3.1 mi), although cruise visitors can concentrate on Samurai Residence Street and shorten the route substantially.

The journey can be done independently when train times line up well, but the port transfer, railway journey and waiting time consume a significant part of the day. Missing a convenient return train can quickly reduce the safety margin.

Independent sightseeing: Reasonable only with careful timetable planning on a long call. Organized excursion recommended when time ashore is limited.

Self-Guided Walking Tours

Easy Port Walk: Cruise Terminal to Selion

Distance: About 2 km (1.2 mi) round trip
Pure walking time: About 25–30 minutes
Recommended total time: 1–1.5 hours
Difficulty: Easy and mostly level.

  1. Akita Cruise Terminal – leave the passenger area and follow the permitted route toward the Selion complex.
  2. Michi-no-Eki Akita Port – browse the local-products area if time permits.
  3. Port Tower Selion – take the elevator to the observation level for views over the harbor and Sea of Japan.
  4. Selion Rista – visit the glass-covered indoor green space beside the tower.
  5. Return to the cruise terminal along the same straightforward port-side route.

This is the safest self-guided choice for passengers with only a short period ashore because the ship remains nearby throughout the visit.

Moderate Central Akita Walk

Start/finish: Akita Station West Exit
Distance: About 4.5 km (2.8 mi)
Pure walking time: About 60–70 minutes
Recommended total time: 3–4 hours including sightseeing stops
Difficulty: Moderate. Central streets are mostly easy, but Senshu Park has slopes and steps.

  1. Akita Station West Exit – the practical starting point after arriving from the cruise port.
  2. Akita Museum of Art – approximately 10 minutes from the station, with its large Tsuguharu Foujita mural among the principal exhibits.
  3. Senshu Park moat – cross toward the former Kubota Castle grounds.
  4. Kubota Castle Main Gate and Osumiyagura – continue uphill through the park. Skip the upper turret if you want a flatter and shorter walk.
  5. Neburinagashi Kan – learn about Akita's Kanto lantern festival and other local performing traditions.
  6. Red Brick Folk Museum – a former bank building containing regional art and craft collections.
  7. Akita Citizen's Market – near the station and useful for local food, seafood and regional products when open.
  8. Akita Station – return here for your bus, taxi or other transfer back to the ship.

Practical Tips

  • Do not treat Akita as a walk-off city-center port. The immediate harbor area is walkable, but the principal downtown attractions are around Akita Station and Senshu Park.
  • If using the Selion public bus, check both the outbound and return departures before starting sightseeing; gaps between services can be significant.
  • Central Akita's sightseeing loop bus can be useful once you are in the city, but walking is often quicker for the compact cluster around Akita Station and Senshu Park.
  • For Kakunodate, reserve enough time for the port-to-station transfer as well as the train journey. A missed connection can remove much of the return margin.
  • For Oga, road transport is much more practical than attempting a multi-stage public-transport journey during a cruise call.
  • Aim to return to the Akita Port area at least 60–90 minutes before your ship's all-aboard time, and allow a larger margin after longer trips such as Kakunodate or Oga.
